content.heading: About Jake Smith
content.eyebrow: Jake Smith never set out to become a wedding celebrant.

children.text: Back in 2007, a couple asked if he’d marry them. One ceremony led to another, and he quickly realised how much he loved walking with couples through such a meaningful moment. What began as a favour grew into a calling: helping people feel calm, understood and genuinely excited about the step they were taking.

Over the years, he’s performed hundreds of weddings across every kind of venue and setting. Jake brings the same steady presence to each one — listening carefully, planning thoughtfully and shaping a ceremony that feels personal rather than scripted. He enjoys every part of the process: the first enquiry, the planning conversations, liaising with photographers and venues, supporting family on the day and, yes, even lodging the paperwork afterwards. It all matters, because it all contributes to a ceremony that feels honest and joyful.

Jake gladly works with couples from all beliefs or none at all. He leads with warmth, integrity and respect — values that help couples feel safe, supported and never judged. Whether you want a ceremony with faith elements or a civil celebration, Jake meets you where you are.

At home, Jake is deeply grateful for his wife, Leone, and their daughters, Abigail and Isabel. Being a husband and father only strengthens his commitment to helping couples build not just a memorable wedding day, but a strong marriage beyond it. He cares about people, he cares about marriage, and he would love to contribute that care to your marriage story.
Don't see your question here? Get in touch, I'm here to help!

questions.question: Are you legally authorised to marry us?
questions.answer: Yes. Jake Smith is an authorised Commonwealth Civil Marriage Celebrant. He can prepare and witness your NOIM, conduct your ceremony, and lodge all paperwork so your marriage is legally registered in Australia.

questions.question: Do you only perform Christian wedding ceremonies?
questions.answer: While Jake is a Christian and an ordained pastor he is a civil celebrant and over half of the weddings he conducts are not religious in any way. He creates warm, relaxed, meaningful ceremonies for couples of any belief or background.

questions.question: How far in advance should we book?
questions.answer: Jake books out early, especially on weekends, unfortunately we have to turn away over 800 couples every year. Most couples enquire 6–18 months in advance however the sooner you enquire, the greater the likelihood of Jake being available for you. If your wedding is happening soon it’s still worth checking — Jake often has midweek availability at short-notice.

questions.question: What is included in your ceremony?
questions.answer: Your ceremony includes an initial and final video chat discussing processes and key moments with you, ceremony preparation and delivery, PA system use, conducting the ceremony and lodging all legal paperwork with the relevant Births, Deaths and Marriages.

questions.question: Do you help with writing vows?
questions.answer: Absolutely. Jake provides guidance, examples, and a simple structure to help you craft vows that feel natural and personal. If writing isn’t your thing, he’ll gently coach you through it.

questions.question: What documents do we need to get married?
questions.answer: You’ll need ID such as a passport or birth certificate plus photo ID. If either of you has been married before, you’ll need evidence of divorce or your previous partner’s death. Jake will guide you through all requirements.

questions.question: When do we need to lodge the NOIM?
questions.answer: The Notice of Intended Marriage must be lodged with Jake at least one month before the wedding date. He’ll help you complete and submit it correctly so everything is legally compliant.

questions.question: Do you do elopements or small weddings?
questions.answer: Yes. Jake loves intimate weddings. Whether it’s the two of you and two witnesses over 18 or a tiny gathering with close family, he’ll create a ceremony that still feels meaningful and well-supported.

questions.question: Will you travel for our wedding?
questions.answer: Jake regularly performs ceremonies across Australia and abroad. He’s based in Brisbane so over half his ceremonies are in South East Queensland, however he flies to over 50 weddings every year, he’d love to help you no matter where you’re getting married!

questions.question: How long does a typical ceremony run?
questions.answer: Most ceremonies run around 18–25 minutes, depending on readings, rituals and how you want the moment to feel. Jake keeps things engaging, personal and well-paced.

questions.question: Do you attend rehearsals?
questions.answer: Jake isn't able to attend on-site rehearsals but you will have a video-chat with Jake to discuss any details of your day.

questions.question: Can we meet you before booking?
questions.answer: Yes. Jake is happy to have a quick video chat so you can make sure he feels like the right fit. There’s no pressure and no obligation — just a friendly conversation.

questions.question: What happens after the wedding?
questions.answer: Jake submits your marriage documents to Births, Deaths and Marriages. You can then order your official marriage certificate directly from BDM in your state once processing is complete.
